lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: sorting by color and fabric

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 2: Clothing and Laundry Care
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice sorting by color and fabric. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: A basket of clean, unsorted laundry from your household is ready to be sorted before its next wash.
materials: learner-local: a basket or pile of clean, unsorted laundry
learner-local: a flat surface to sort on
learner-local: paper or a notes app to record your groupings

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain one specific reason a fabric-type sort catches a risk that a color-only sort would miss, using the tricky item from your pile as your example.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Sorting accuracy: The full pile is correctly sorted by both color and fabric type in two separate, complete passes. | Reasoning about the tricky item: The explanation names a specific risk, such as dye transfer or shrinking, tied to the item and the rule that matters most for it. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a third sorting pass by wash-temperature safety (items that can only go in cool water versus items that can handle warm water) and identify any item that lands in a different combination across all three groupings, explaining what that overlap means for how they'd actually run that load.

resources.title: sorting by color and fabric worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: A basket of clean, unsorted laundry from your household is ready to be sorted before its next wash.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact sorting by color and fabric decision or action.
Model move 2: Before sorting, look through the whole pile once without moving anything.
Model move 3: Sort the pile into three color groups: light, dark, and bright or patterned.

Model check: Sorting accuracy: The full pile is correctly sorted by both color and fabric type in two separate, complete passes. | Reasoning about the tricky item: The explanation names a specific risk, such as dye transfer or shrinking, tied to the item and the rule that matters most for it.

resources.title: sorting by color and fabric coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: A basket of clean, unsorted laundry from your household is ready to be sorted before its next wash.
Coach direction: Before sorting, look through the whole pile once without moving anything.
Learner prompt: Name one item in the pile that you think will be tricky to sort, and guess which group or groups it might belong to.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: sorting by color and fabric complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Sort the pile into three color groups: light, dark, and bright or patterned. Then, without mixing those groups back together, sort the same pile again into two fabric groups: sturdy (like jeans, towels, sweatshirts) and delicate (like thin knits, lace, or stretch mesh).
Response 1 (t2-p1): I sorted the whole pile into three color groups before starting the fabric sort.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I sorted the same items into sturdy and delicate fabric groups.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I kept notes on which items ended up in different-seeming groups between the two sorts.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: sorting by color and fabric minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific reason a fabric-type sort catches a risk that a color-only sort would miss, using the tricky item from your pile as your example.

Success checks: Sorting accuracy: The full pile is correctly sorted by both color and fabric type in two separate, complete passes. | Reasoning about the tricky item: The explanation names a specific risk, such as dye transfer or shrinking, tied to the item and the rule that matters most for it.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: sorting by color and fabric supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional sorting by color and fabric condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Sorting accuracy: The full pile is correctly sorted by both color and fabric type in two separate, complete passes. | Reasoning about the tricky item: The explanation names a specific risk, such as dye transfer or shrinking, tied to the item and the rule that matters most for it..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u02-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
